# CJSW Friends — the data

Every business in [CJSW 90.9 FM](https://cjsw.com)'s Friends of CJSW discount program,
with its location, its offer and enough structure to build a client on. **203 locations,
152 businesses, all in and around Calgary, Alberta.**

These files are generated from a working repo and published here whole, so they are
safe to consume and pointless to patch — an edit here would be overwritten by the next
refresh. Corrections are welcome as issues.

| File | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `friends.json` | The records. One object per physical location. |
| `friends.csv` | The same rows, flat, for spreadsheets and quick imports. |
| `categories.json` | The 26 categories, the 10 families they roll up into, and each family's label, colour and icon. |
| `areas.json` | The areas a location can filter under, the district circles, and the rule that resolves them. |

## Reading it

Nothing here needs a parser beyond your language's JSON. The shape, as Kotlin:

```kotlin
@Serializable
data class Friend(
    val id: Int,
    val name: String,
    val deal: String,
    val category: String,
    val neighbourhood: String,      // ignore this one — see the table below
    val area: String? = null,
    val address: String? = null,
    val website: String? = null,
    val latitude: Double? = null,
    val longitude: Double? = null,
    val phone: String? = null,
    val placeID: String? = null,
    val photo: String? = null,
)

val friends = Json { ignoreUnknownKeys = true }
    .decodeFromString<List<Friend>>(assets.open("friends.json").reader().readText())
```

Keep `ignoreUnknownKeys` on: a later refresh may add a field, and it should not break you.

## One record per location, not per business

23 businesses have more than one address, so `Phil and Sebastian Coffee Roasters` is nine
records. A map pin and a discount are per address, so that is the unit.

`id` is `wordpressPostId * 100 + locationIndex`. Divide by 100 to group a chain back
together — that is the only reliable way, since the names carry a disambiguating suffix.
Ids are stable between yearly refreshes as long as the source keeps its location order.

## Fields

Every key is present on every record. `null` means "not known", never "empty".

| Field | Type | Present | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | int | 203/203 | See above. Stable; safe as a primary key. |
| `name` | string | 203/203 | A multi-location business gets its street appended: `Purr (940 17 Ave SW)`. |
| `deal` | string | 203/203 | The offer, verbatim. `Friends Card discount` is the fallback when the source gives no detail — treat it as "unspecified". |
| `category` | string | 203/203 | One of the 26 in `categories.json`. |
| `neighbourhood` | string | 203/203 | **Don't use this.** The source's own tag: 28 free-text values, 67 records carry the literal string `No Address`, and the ones that exist are not geographically coherent. Kept only because it is in the upstream payload. Use `area` / `areas.json`. |
| `area` | string \| null | 20/203 | A hand-assigned override for the area a record belongs to. `null` — the usual case — means "work it out from the coordinate", per `areas.json`. |
| `address` | string | 203/203 | Free text as entered upstream. Formatting is inconsistent; the coordinates are the reliable location. |
| `website` | string \| null | 198/203 | Normalised to `https://` where the host supports it, tracking parameters stripped. |
| `latitude` / `longitude` | float \| null | 203/203 | WGS84. From Google Places via the source CMS, with hand corrections. Precise enough for a 100 m geofence. |
| `phone` | string \| null | 176/203 | Digits as entered — no formatting, no country code, occasionally with punctuation. |
| `placeID` | string \| null | 198/203 | Google Places id, resolved by business name, not by address geocode. Use it to fetch hours, rating and open/closed live. |
| `photo` | string \| null | 143/203 | The business's own `og:image`. Collected but unused: about half are logos or banners rather than photos of the place. Quality varies; check before shipping it. |

### Two things that will bite you

**Hours, ratings and open/closed are deliberately absent.** Google's terms let you store
`place_id` and nothing else, so a client fetches those live per record and throws them
away. That is why `placeID` is here and a `hours` field is not.

**`photo` URLs may be `http://`.** They are upgraded where the host answers on TLS, but
some do not. Android blocks cleartext by default, which is the correct behaviour.

## Categories

`categories.json` gives the whole taxonomy:

```json
"families":    [{ "id": "dining", "label": "Restaurants", "shortLabel": "Restaurants",
                  "icon": "fork.knife", "colour": "#E67021" }, …],
"categories":  { "Restaurants & Bars": { "family": "dining", "icon": "fork.knife" }, … }
```

**Filter by family, draw by category.** Ten families is a usable filter; 26 categories is
not. Colour comes from the family so the map reads at a glance, and the icon comes from the
category so a brewery and a liquor store still differ. `icon` values are SF Symbol names —
they are labels, not assets. Map them to your own icon set.

If a category is not in the table (a future refresh can add one), lowercase it and take the
first match in `fallbackKeywords`; if nothing matches, the family is `other`.

## Areas

`areas.json` describes the geography filter. Resolution order for a record:

1. its own `area` field, if set;
2. the first district in `districts` whose circle contains its coordinate;
3. the quadrant named in its `address` (`NW`, `NE`, `SW`, `SE`) — last match in the string wins;
4. the quadrant its coordinate falls in, split at `quadrantOrigin`.

`Other` is hand-assignment only. Blindman Brewing is in Lacombe, 150 km north — the
quadrant rule calls that "NE", which is true of the compass and a lie about the
neighbourhood.

Districts are circles rather than boundaries because they are also the app's geofences.
Where a circle gets a district wrong — downtown ends at the river and the rail line, not at
a 600 m radius — the record carries an explicit `area` instead. That is what those 20 are.

## Provenance, and what is not here

Scraped from CJSW's public WordPress API (`cjsw_friends` post type), then enriched: place
ids resolved by name through Google Places Text Search, `og:image` fetched from each
business's own site, and a review pass by hand for category and location errors. Every hand
correction is recorded separately from the scraped value, so upstream's version and ours
can always be told apart.

Businesses found to have closed are removed, with the reason recorded, so a re-scrape
cannot resurrect them.

**Refreshed each October**, when CJSW's funding drive renews the Friends list. A record can
disappear between refreshes; `id` will not be reused.

The offers are CJSW's to give, not ours — you need a current Friends card to use one. This
is a copy of a public listing, published so other clients can exist, and it comes with no
warranty that any given discount is still on.
